purpose: Sertraline is used to help treat depression, anxiety, panic attacks, and obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD), among other conditions. It can help improve your mood, sleep, energy, and overall sense of wellbeing. It may also be used for post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) and social anxiety disorder.
how_it_works: Your brain uses a chemical called serotonin to help regulate mood and emotions. Sertraline works by keeping more serotonin available in your brain for longer, which helps lift your mood and reduce anxiety. Think of it like keeping a helpful chemical from being cleared away too quickly.
common_side_effects: Nausea, upset stomach, diarrhea, dry mouth, trouble sleeping or feeling sleepy, dizziness, sweating, and decreased sex drive are the most common side effects. These often improve after the first few weeks as your body adjusts to the medication.
warnings: Do not stop taking sertraline suddenly without talking to your doctor, as this can cause withdrawal symptoms. It may increase thoughts of self-harm in some young people, especially in the first few weeks, so contact your doctor right away if this happens. Avoid alcohol while taking this medication. Tell your doctor about all other medications you take, as some combinations can be dangerous.
typical_dosing: Most adults start at 25 to 50 mg once daily, usually in the morning or evening. Your doctor may gradually increase the dose up to 200 mg per day depending on how you respond. It can take 4 to 6 weeks to feel the full benefit, so be patient and keep taking it as prescribed.
